correctness.rationale: Rational independence of relative one-particle gaps equidistributes the time phases on the vertex torus. Expanding X=sum r_e(exp(iΔtheta+iφ)+exp(-iΔtheta-iφ)) shows only zero-incidence signed edge multisets survive. Counting connected contributions at orders 2,3,4 yields κ2=2∑r², κ3=12∑_triangles ∏r cosΦ, κ4=-6∑r⁴+48∑_4cycles ∏r cosΦ. Every forest oriented-incidence matrix extends to unimodular root-plus-edge coordinates, so edge difference phases are jointly independent Haar; any cycle has a nontrivial modular relation, hence iff forest. Thus forest law is sum of 2r cos Θ, characteristic function ∏J0(2rs), and Berry–Esseen with exact third-absolute-moment prefactor 8√2/(3π). Fresh independent exact rational signed-edge enumeration on a graph with triangle and four-cycle gave κ2=28/5, κ3=189/50, κ4=-8031/1250 and matched the predicted formula; finite checks corroborate general incidence proof.
residual_risks: Requires all integer relative gaps independent and number-conserving quasifree setting; resonances add terms. Forest needed for independent cosines and finite-size normal bound; cyclic systems may still be Gaussian by other mechanisms.

value.rationale: Theorem connects explicit graph topology to non-Gaussian temporal skewness/kurtosis and gives a sharp structural independence criterion for whole forest families, plus a finite-size Gaussian-equilibration bound. These are motivated, mathematically reusable conclusions beyond standard independent-summand BE applied to an already-factorized toy example.
residual_risks: Fourth-order cycle enumeration is elementary once XY mapping is granted; its value derives from precise general class and iff forest boundary rather than alleged novelty of Fourier moment technique.

scientific_limitations: Finite one-particle dimension; 0≤R≤I; Hermitian quadratic a; all relative gaps rationally independent; independent sum/BE only acyclic active graph; no pairing Hamiltonians.
